title: MistralWorks — Model selection, context length & tool-calling deployment scout
summary: Intro discovery focused on model choice for a multilingual customer-facing assistant, strict latency and data residency constraints, exploring Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Customer needs long context (>=64k tokens for long docs + retrieval), tool-calling to internal search and RAG, SOC2 and KMS requirements. SE offered benchmarking plan and suggested pilot using Redwood Hosted with Dedicated fallback and Private for sensitive flows.
topics: tool-calling and retrieval architecture (RAG, DB connectors)
deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
security: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
action_items: Samira Patel: Share TCO spreadsheet comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private including GPU and quantization assumptions - due 2026-04-03

Priya Nair: Provide sample doc corpus and example queries (anonymized) for RAG evaluation - due 2026-04-05

Customer to send sample corpus and success criteria

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Clarke (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (CTO, MistralWorks), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Ola Svensson (Infra), Marco Li (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, drill into model choices and deployment constraints. Customer very concerned about data residency for PII, but wants fast iteration. Discussed long-context options and tool calling for internal search + actions.

00:00:03 - Samira (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. That's Samira and Evan from Redwood. How's everyone doing?
00:00:10 - Diego (CTO): Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get into the options.
00:00:18 - Samira: Great. High level — you sent over the one-pager that said multilingual support, long doc handling and tool calling. Can you confirm priorities?
00:00:26 - Marco (Product): Yeah, prioritization is: 1) accurate multilingual responses (EN/ES/FR/JA), 2) ability to call internal search and ticketing tools, 3) low tail latency for interactive features. Cost is important but we can trade some cost for latency.
00:00:40 - Evan (SE): Quick clarifying question — when you say long doc handling, what's the typical doc size and how much context do you want the model to see in a single pass?
00:00:48 - Priya (ML Eng): We're seeing multi-chapter spec docs, sometimes >200k characters. Practically we'd like 64k token window for a decent RAG + in-session context. 32k is a minimum for some flows but 64k preferred.
00:01:02 - Ola (Infra): We also have data residency requirements for EU customers. Anything with PII needs to stay in their EU region and be encrypted with our KMS.
00:01:12 - Samira: Got it. So long-context plus region controls and KMS. That's exactly where Redwood's Hosted/Dedicated/Private choices come into play. Evan, want to cover deployment modes briefly?
00:01:22 - Evan: Sure. Hosted is fastest to get started — you can spin up models from our catalog, we manage the infra. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput and is good if you need steady high throughput or want dedicated capacity. Private (VPC or on-prem) brings the control plane into your VPC or a package we deploy on-prem for air-gapped. For EU residency + KMS you could do Hosted in our EU region with customer-managed KMS or go Dedicated/Private for stricter isolation.
00:01:55 - Priya: If we go Hosted in EU, how do you handle logs and KV cache? Can Redwood ensure KV cache doesn't cross regions?
00:02:05 - Evan: Yes, we have region pinning for runtime and KV cache. One note — sometimes the KV cache gets transcribed as KV cash — sorry that's my brain — but region pinning is supported.
00:02:16 - Diego: (laughs) important note.
00:02:20 - Samira: Let's talk model choices. You're evaluating open models — what did you look at?
00:02:28 - Priya: We evaluated a few: Llama-based variants, Mistral 8x/22B style models, and some newer instruction-tuned families. We care about multilingual quality and latency. We're also curious about quantized variants for cost.
00:02:42 - Evan: Ok. For multilingual and long context, two axes: model architecture (how it handles cross-lingual pretraining) and context window support. Some models offer efficient 64k or more via sparse attention or custom kernels. Redwood's runtime supports optimized kernels and quantized execution paths. For 64k you might see latency increase — we can run benchmarks.
00:03:06 - Marco: Tool-calling — we need the model to call internal search, ticketing (Jira), and possibly a payment API for actions. How does Redwood support tool calling and safety?
00:03:18 - Evan: We have structured tool-calling primitives and function calling support in the API. You can declare tool schemas, and we do response validation. For safety, you can route tool calls through a middleware that enforces RBAC and audit logging. In Dedicated/Private you can push that middleware into your network perimeter.
00:03:40 - Priya: Any differences in latency for tool-calling between Hosted vs Dedicated?
00:03:44 - Evan: Dedicated avoids noisy neighbors and gives predictable tail latency. Hosted is multi-tenant but we have SLOs; you might see slightly higher p99s in peak. Private on-prem gives you the fastest path if you control the network.
00:03:55 - Diego: What's the typical throughput on a Dedicated pool for a 22B model at 64k? I'm trying to budget concurrency.
00:04:04 - Evan: Good question. Ballpark: single A100-dense node with optimized kernels could handle X tokens/sec depending on batching and sequence length. We'll run a benchmark matrix — we'll include throughput at 2k/8k/32k/64k windows and show tokens/sec and p50/p95/p99 latency.
00:04:20 - Samira: We'll include quantized configs too (8-bit/4-bit) for cost tradeoffs.
00:04:26 - Marco: On privacy — SOC 2 Type II is required. Do you have ISO? We also need audit logs for model access at token level.
00:04:35 - Samira: We are SOC 2 compliant; we can share the attestation. We also provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns and audit logs. For encryption we support customer KMS integrations — HSM is on the roadmap for Private customers.
00:04:48 - Ola: How about SSO/SAML and RBAC?
00:04:52 - Samira: SSO via SAML/OIDC and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. For Private we can integrate with your IdP behind the VPC.
00:04:59 - Diego: Back to models — any Redwood recommendations for multilingual + long context out of the box? We're open to using Mistral-like families if the instruction tuning for ES/JA is good.
00:05:12 - Evan: For pure multilingual quality, some family variants with multi-lingual pretraining outperform English-only models. Another path: use an English-primed model with translation pre/post-processing. But if you want end-to-end in ES/JA, look at models with multilingual corpora. We'll share a shortlist: 1) LlamaX-multi-XX (if available), 2) Mistral-Long-* variants, 3) Falcon-multi variants. We'll also include instruction-tuned vs base tradeoffs.
00:05:39 - Priya: We also need support for function/tool-calling that returns structured payloads (JSON schemas) to drive our ticketing flows.
00:05:47 - Evan: Yes, our function-calling supports schema validation and we can attach a safety layer that sanitizes inputs. On Dedicated/Private you can host the middleware to enforce enterprise policies.
00:05:58 - Marco: In terms of cost, do you have quick numbers for token cost for 64k contexts vs 8k? It's a big driver for choosing model and quantization.
00:06:08 - Samira: We'll send a TCO with sample rates. Roughly, longer context increases per-call compute and memory so cost goes up non-linearly. Quantization can reduce model memory footprint and improve cost, but there are quality tradeoffs; we'll show quality delta in a benchmark.
00:06:22 - Diego: Ok, what's the pilot you suggest?
00:06:25 - Evan: Two-phase: 1) Hosted quick pilot — we onboard you onto Hosted with EU region pinning, load your anonymized docs, run RAG and tool-calling flows for 2 weeks; measure latency and quality. 2) If successful or if you need isolation, move to Dedicated pilot with reserved GPUs and then evaluate Private for the most sensitive flows.
00:06:42 - Priya: That sounds reasonable. For the Hosted trial, will the KV cache persist across restarts and how is it encrypted?
00:06:50 - Evan: KV cache persists per runtime in the region; encryption at rest is supported and you can plug in your KMS for Hosted EU. If you require full control we recommend Dedicated or Private.
00:07:00 - Ola: Networking: for Private, do you offer an on-prem appliance or is it a container package?
00:07:07 - Evan: We have a Private package that can be deployed behind your firewall; depending on requirements we can do a VPC private endpoint or an on-prem kit. We'll need to scope the networking ports and egress rules.
00:07:18 - Marco: Any known model regressions with retrieval when you increase context to 64k? We've seen hallucination drift with some long-window runs.
00:07:26 - Evan: Yes, longer contexts can increase retrieval noise. We recommend fine-tuned reranker and prompt engineering, and Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/caching and quantization profiles. We'll tie regressions to evaluation prompt sets and alert on quality drops.
00:07:42 - Diego: Are there customers using 100k+ context with Redwood?
00:07:46 - Samira: A few pilot customers are experimenting with 100k+ via chunked processing and KV layering; it's more complex but doable with the right kernels and batching. We'll include notes in the benchmark about feasibility.
00:07:57 - Priya: For multilingual evaluation, can you run bilingual evals? We need Spanish/Japanese corpora checked.
00:08:04 - Evan: Yes we'll run multilingual evals and include BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics and qualitative checks. We'll capture latency per-language too since tokenization affects token count.
00:08:15 - (brief pause)
00:08:20 - Marco: Ok, let's talk timing — goal is a pilot within the next 3 weeks. Is that realistic?
00:08:25 - Samira: Yes. If you can send anon corpus and success KPIs this week, we can scope a Hosted pilot next week.
00:08:32 - Diego: We'll try to get data to you by Friday.
00:08:35 - Samira: Great. A couple of quick questions from me — any regulatory constraints beyond EU data residency?
00:08:41 - Ola: We have some healthcare customers in the EU — need audit trails, data masking, and occasionally on-prem for PHI.
00:08:49 - Samira: Noted. We'll flag Private as the PHI path.
00:08:53 - Priya: One more: we use an internal vector DB (OpenSearch + custom plugins). Does Redwood integrate with external vector stores or do you require your RAG to use your onboard store?
00:09:03 - Evan: We support connectors to external vector stores (OpenSearch, Pinecone, Milvus) and can integrate with your custom plugin via an adapter. For Hosted we can host retrieval nodes in your region and index. For Private you can keep indexes entirely inside your VPC.
00:09:18 - Marco: Perfect. Anything else on tooling?
00:09:22 - Evan: We'll capture tool schemas and show an example of function calling with a Jira create-ticket flow. We'll also demo structured outputs so your product UI can render actions.
00:09:33 - (crosstalk)
00:09:36 - Diego: Regarding cost of Dedicated — do you offer burst capacity for spiky workloads?
00:09:41 - Evan: Yes, Dedicated can be configured with burst capacity and autoscaling policies. We can set cold/warm pools and configure pre-warming.
00:09:49 - Samira: Ok let's recap next steps — Diego send corpus + KPIs; Samira/Evan send TCO + benchmark plan; schedule pilot kickoff.
00:09:59 - Diego: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
00:10:03 - Samira: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with links to the security docs and SOC 2 report.
00:10:08 - Marco: Quick note — please include example function schemas for payments and ticket creation, those will help Priya.
00:10:15 - Evan: Will do.
00:10:18 - (call ends, recording continues for notes)

Notes about transcript quality: some speaker labels are approximate; occasional word errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "MistralWorks" transcribed as "Mistral works").

References shared: https://redwood.example.com/decks/mistralworks-pilot (redwood pilot deck), TCO spreadsheet (link to be sent), security-attestation.pdf (SOC2)
